purpose: Preserve statistical source semantics and prevent descriptive police-contact variables from being promoted into legal conclusions without qualifying evidence.

research_pointer.note: The media item is a discovery trigger only. It is not national prevalence evidence and does not establish lawful self-defense.

reviewed_sources.title: Contacts Between Police and the Public, 2022
semantic_boundary: Measures reported police contact and respondent perceptions.
Does not by itself establish whether force was legally justified or whether civilian force was lawful self-defense.

reviewed_sources.title: National Use-of-Force Data Collection
semantic_boundary: The FBI states that this collection does not assess or report whether officers acted lawfully or followed department policy.
Resistance, threat, or weapon-involvement variables are descriptive and cannot be promoted to a legal conclusion by this register.

reviewed_sources.title: Law Enforcement Officers Assaulted, 2024
reviewed_sources.status_note: The May 2025 special report describes 2024 assault data as preliminary and subject to change before later LEOKA tables.
semantic_boundary: Officer-assault reporting is not equivalent to a legal finding that a civilian committed an unlawful attack.
This source alone cannot identify lawful civilian self-defense against police.

bounded_gap_finding.claim: No direct variable for legally established civilian self-defense against police was identified in the reviewed BJS PPCS, FBI National Use-of-Force, and FBI LEOKA source families.
